description: The provided chart is a multi-layered donut or radial visualization from the paper “Can Language Models Follow Multiple Turns of Entangled Instructions,” illustrating the distribution of various capabilities or tasks evaluated in the study. The chart is divided into three main inner segments labeled “Contradiction Resolution,” “Context Tracking,” and “Context Retrieving,” each representing a core competency area. Surrounding these are ten outer segments, each corresponding to a specific task or feature, with numerical values indicating their relative weight or frequency: “Prioritization (100),” “Personalization (100),” “Privacy Protection (111),” “Multitasking (160),” “Dynamic Instruction (100),” “Memorization (100),” “Dynamic Environment (100),” “Recursive Reasoning (110),” “Triggering (100),” and “Prioritization (100)” again (possibly a duplicate label). The segments are color-coded in shades of red, blue, and green, with the largest segment being “Multitasking” at 160, followed by “Privacy Protection” and “Recursive Reasoning.” The chart visually emphasizes the relative importance or prevalence of each capability within the context of entangled instruction following, with “Multitasking” being the most prominent, suggesting it plays a central or more frequently tested role in the evaluation framework. The inner rings likely group these tasks by their underlying cognitive or functional category, offering a hierarchical view of the model’s evaluated competencies.
